senses.gloss: (by ref. to ונקלה, Deut. XXV, 3) to disgrace (one’s self), to have loose bowels; to collapse under the lashes.
units: <cite ref="Makkot 23a:17">Macc. 23ᵃ</cite> <he>ק׳ בין בראשונה וכ׳</he> if he collapses either at the first or at the second lash, he must be released. Tosef. ib. V (IV), 14 <he>אם קי׳ באחד מהן</he> if he collapsed at one of them.
<cite ref="Makkot 23a:17">Ib.</cite> <he>ק׳ עד שלא לקה</he> if he collapsed (from fear) before receiving lashes.

<cite ref="Makkot 23a:17">Ib.</cite> <he>אמדוהו שאם ילקה וקי׳</he> (Var. <he>יקלקל</he>) if the experts opine that he will collapse, when he is lashed; <he>שאם יוצא מב״ד קי׳</he> (Var. <he>וקלקל</he>) that he will collapse on leaving the court; Macc. l. c. <he>יְקַלֶּה</he> Ms. M. (or <he>יִקָּלֶה</he>; ed. <he>קלה</he>). Ib. <he>והכהו … ולא שיקלה כבר וכ׳</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>שלקה</he>, corr. acc.; Var. <he>שנִקְלָה</he>) we read, ‘lest if he should exceed …, thy brother be disgraced’, but he must not be beaten at all, if he has collapsed in court ere this; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 937:14">Yalk. Deut. 937</cite> <he>שנקלה וכ׳</he>; a. e.

senses.gloss: to be disgraced. Ib. כפתוהו … מ״ט ונקלה והא נ׳ if he runs away from court after they have tied him, he is released; why? The text says, v’niḳlah, and he has been disgraced; Macc. l. c. Ms. M. (not in ed.), v. supra; a. e.
